Ich erstelle Investmentmemos, bereite die Entscheidungsgrundlagen für das Investmentkomitee auf und begleite darüber hinaus die strategische Weiterentwicklung ausgewählter Portfoliounternehmen. Ziel meiner Arbeit ist es, innovative, tragfähige und zukunftsfähige Unternehmen mit nachhaltigem Wachstumspotenzial frühzeitig zu identifizieren und zu skalieren.

Following AT&T’s acquisition of FirstComm, I joined the company to help scale and modernize its international network capabilities—operating at a level of complexity and scale far beyond startup environments.

- Building the AT&T Global Network (AGN): Spearheaded the development and deployment of the global IP-VPN network, leading a globally distributed organization of approximately 4,000 to define and execute the network’s technical foundation.

- Aligning strategy with execution: Established the technical framework that translated business objectives into scalable, resilient infrastructure across regions and regulatory environments.

- Technology innovation: Led the creation and rollout of IP/Ethernet access technologies that became central to AT&T’s ability to deliver reliable, high-performance global connectivity.

- Operating at extreme scale: Managed systems where uptime, security, and performance were non-negotiable—shaping my approach to risk, architecture, and long-term system design.

This experience grounded my understanding of what it truly takes to operate technology at a global scale—and continues to inform how I design, build, and prioritize systems today.

- Operationalizing speed at enterprise scale: Reworked product and engineering processes to increase delivery velocity while maintaining reliability and security demanded by large global customers.

- Customer-led product strategy: Partnered closely with customers and go-to-market teams to accelerate adoption of new capabilities, sharpen value propositions, and address complex, real-world technology management challenges.

- Leading globally distributed teams: Built and guided high-performing, international product organizations—improving software lifecycle agility, decision clarity, and return on R&D investment.

This chapter deepened my experience operating at scale—bridging founder-led innovation with enterprise execution—and reinforced my conviction that the next wave of meaningful software progress will come from rethinking foundational assumptions.

- Cross-functional fluency: Advanced quickly through roles that bridged go-to-market, product definition, and deep technical research—building the ability to translate between engineers, executives, and customers.

- Technology strategy: I helped envision the future of networking by guiding the design, evaluation, and adoption of foundational technologies with long-term industry impact.

- From research to reality: Worked at the intersection of innovation and execution—ensuring that Bell Labs–level breakthroughs could be operationalized, scaled, and aligned with real-world business needs.

- Strategic technology leadership: Applied business and market insight to prioritize investments, acquisitions, and internal initiatives that shaped Lucent’s R&D networking roadmap.

- Culture of rigor and curiosity: Immersed in an environment where ideas were stress-tested, assumptions were challenged, and durability mattered more than hype.

This experience instilled the intellectual discipline and systems-level thinking that continue to guide how I evaluate problems, design architectures, and build companies from the ground up.

Founded NOX following my first successful exit to back and build early-stage companies—particularly those led by overlooked founders—by pairing capital with hands-on operational support.

Over a decade, I shaped NOX into an operator-led angel investment platform focused on turning fragile early ideas into durable, execution-ready businesses in underserved communities. My role extended well beyond capital allocation, encompassing strategy, product direction, financial discipline, and founder coaching.

Key focus areas and impact:

- Operator-first investing: Worked closely with entrepreneurs to strengthen core fundamentals—unit economics, go-to-market clarity, and operational rigor—rather than relying on capital alone.

- Scaling founder capability: Mentored and advised founders in underserved communities, helping them professionalize execution, improve fiscal discipline, and build sustainable operating models.

- Intentional transition: Concluded my work at NOX in 2017 to pursue a conviction-led opportunity that became MetaPort.

This chapter fundamentally shaped my approach to company-building—reinforcing that long-term success comes from strong foundations, disciplined execution, and founder empathy, not just speed or capital.

Founded and bootstrapped MetaPort to solve a deeply persistent problem in enterprise telecom: the lack of real-time visibility into complex, distributed network and cost structures.

Starting from first principles, I designed and built an enterprise-grade network mapping SaaS platform that unified inventory, cost, and network intelligence into a single, continuously updated system of record—giving organizations unprecedented clarity and control over their telecom environments.

Key milestones and impact:

- Zero-to-scale execution: Bootstrapped MetaPort from concept to production adoption, securing Fortune 1000 customers by delivering immediate, measurable operational value.

- Category-defining innovation: Created a novel approach to network visualization that fundamentally changed how enterprises understand and manage network complexity.

- Industry recognition: MetaPort was named “Coolest New Technology in the Networking Space” by Gartner, validating both the technical innovation and market relevance.

- Strategic acquisition: Led MetaPort through its acquisition by Calero in 2022, transitioning the technology from a standalone product into a core component of a global Technology Expense Management platform.

- Founder-to-operator transition: Joined Calero post-acquisition to integrate and scale MetaPort’s capabilities across a much larger customer base—bridging startup innovation with enterprise execution.

This experience sharpened my conviction that the most impactful software companies are built by identifying overlooked problems, questioning long-standing assumptions, and obsessively focusing on foundational systems that others accept as “good enough.”

FirstComm, one of the early international Competitive Local Exchange Carrier (CLEC) startups, where I led technology strategy and execution during a period of rapid global expansion.

At FirstComm, I was Co-founder and responsible for designing and scaling the technical foundation of a fiber-optic–driven telecom services business—ensuring that infrastructure decisions directly supported commercial growth, reliability, and long-term competitiveness.

Key contributions and outcomes:

 - First-principles infrastructure design: Built and scaled core telecom and fiber-optic systems in highly regulated, capital-intensive environments—developing an early appreciation for the cost, complexity, and durability required of foundational technology.

- Technology–business alignment: Translated business objectives into executable technology roadmaps, ensuring product and network investments supported revenue growth and market expansion.

- Global scale execution: Led technical expansion across Latin America, Europe, and Asia, navigating operational, regulatory, and integration challenges inherent in international telecom markets.

- Stakeholder communication: Regularly communicated technology strategy and tradeoffs to partners, customers, and investors—building trust and enabling informed decision-making.

- Successful acquisition: Helped guide FirstComm through its acquisition by AT&T, marking my first experience scaling a startup into a strategic enterprise outcome.

This experience established the foundation for my career—shaping my approach to building resilient systems, aligning technology with real business needs, and operating effectively at the intersection of infrastructure, scale, and execution.

current.employer_linkedin_description: MissionBrightday’s mission is to deliver next-generation software products that promote health and focus during the workday. The founders’ vision is to fundamentally improve the modern workplace, creating healthier work-life habits through technology. Industry OverviewErgonomics (Latin for “the laws of work”) is a concept developed during the Industrial Revolution. As workplaces moved from factories to offices, cubicle ergonomics evolved to reduce office injuries. However, during the last decade, a shift toward a mobile workforce has allowed people to work from the office, cafe, even the couch. At the same time, corporate wellness trends have increased awareness about the importance of a healthy workplace—no longer just a “nice to have.”Company BackgroundIn 2016, wellness entrepreneur Richard Gray, and product innovator Jens-Peter Jungclaussen, began collaborating on ideas for a posture and wellness start-up. One day, they had an epiphany—instead of furniture or wearables, they could use computer software to teach posture and movement—thus helping users change behavior and develop lifelong habits. Initial work was done with computer vision experts at U Penn before adding software engineer Jim Morris to the team. Working with worldwide research partners and posture experts, they began development.ProductUsing AI and augmented reality, Brightday monitors and improves posture and encourages healthy movement while at the computer. Based on the research of Jean Couch (posture advisor to Kaiser Permanente, Stanford & Google), Brightday uses bite-sized learning to easily ingrain good posture into the user’s routine. Each session focuses on one aspect of posture, first providing a quick training video. Brightday then uses the computer’s webcam to assess the user’s position and guide them back to good posture. Brightday works on all post-2011 laptops/desktops, teaching better posture without significant time or effort, producing immediately noticeable benefits.

past.employer_linkedin_description: The education of women in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia has received a great deal of attention and this has allowed Saudi women to make definite strides towards achieving their ambitions and unveiling their uniqueness in different fields. The Saudi woman has emerged, not only at the local level, but at the international level as well. We see examples of Saudi women in the fields of culture and specialized research, examples who are respected and acknowledged in international arenas and in the various fields of science, proving their success and their worthiness that rivals that of their peers in other advanced countries.  PNU is one of the outcomes of the attention given to the higher education of women. This attention started early, when the General Presidency for the Education of Girls established the first college for women in 1390 AH, corresponding to 1970 CE. The inauguration of more colleges followed, reaching 102, ranging from university colleges to intermediary colleges and community colleges. These were distributed over 72 Saudi cities and included 600,000 students. In Riyadh alone there are six colleges; namely the College of Education for Liberal Arts Disciplines, the College of Education for Scientific Disciplines, the College of Education for the Development of Teachers, the College of Social Services, the College of Home Economics and the College of Fine Arts. In 1427 AH, a royal order was issued for the establishment of the first university for women in Riyadh, under the supervision of the Ministry of Higher Education. This included the six colleges located in Riyadh, in addition to a number of new colleges established for the purpose of women's education and development in the Kingdom. The university was inaugurated in 1428 AH with the appointment of its first rector, H.H. Dr. Al-Jawhara bint Fahd Al-Saud.

past.employer_linkedin_description: MOE Ministry of Education, Saudi ArabiaHistory:A formal education system took shape in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia when the General Education Management Center was established in Ramadan, 1344H, which laid out the first plan for a complete educational system. On 27 Muharram, 1346H, an Education Management Committee was formed which established a single system of education, with different educational levels. The first primary curriculum was designed by 1354H. During 1357H a private school system was also formalized.The Ministry of Education was formed in 1373H. The first education minister in the Kingdom was the late Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, Fahd Bin Abd AlAziz.The most significant achievements of the Ministry in its initial days were:   1. Creation of an administration plan for the Ministry of Education.   2. Construction of schools and continually improving the standards of education.   3. Laying the foundations of higher education with the inauguration of the King Saud University in RiyadhAims:   1. To provide opportunities for education to every citizen of learning age, according to his abilities and inclinations, and to facilitate these opportunities by providing the appropriate infrastructure and services.   2. To design and execute projects that cater to the requirements of the Ministry such as construction of educational buildings, and renovation of existing educational sites, by investing capital sums in the private sector for the implementation of such projects.   3. To improve the curriculum and constantly upgrade the general education system so that it is in accordance with contemporary societal and industry requirements.

M2 is a Storytelling Company that I make deals, manage partnerships and produce content with.

We love great stories. From ancient cave paintings to a galaxy far, far away, we can't get enough of fascinating characters and gripping narratives. We love to consume them and, even better, we are madly in love with creating them.

We are also the fortunate benefactors of the evolving content consumption landscape. We have arrived at a time and place where a screen is a screen is a screen. Be it via mobile phone or multi-plex, the audience has become a savvy consumer of quality story. So much so, they no longer see the distinction between a TV story or a film story, an animation story or a comic book story or a game story. If it's available where and when they want it they will engage and consume. If we do our job as tellers of great story, they transform to the ultimate form of audience member : a fan.

The genius of all this is a new freedom to tell stories and craft experiences that live everywhere the audience is - which is everywhere. Indeed, we focus completely on character and story, utilizing any or all of the available platforms to deepen the audience experience. This is where we as M2 thrive. We look at all facets of the story, then skillfully select the ideal methods of delivering each component of that story and finally execute with passion and intent. 

Our mission is to pioneer rich new experiences that allow our audience to delve deeply into the worlds we create, join us there and kick and scream at any whisper of leaving.

After all, at the end of the day, as consumer or creator, we just want to hear a good story.

basic_profile.name: Kishore N.
basic_profile.headline: Principal Consultant at stealth mode Startup
basic_profile.summary: Twenty-five years in financial technology teaches you one thing: the hardest problems are never purely technical. I've worked across banking operations, core banking transformation, enterprise product management, engineering leadership, and AI programme delivery. Each chapter has been genuinely different. That range is deliberate and I think it makes me more useful, not harder to categorise. I started my career inside a bank. That shaped how I think about technology. It has to work reliably in regulated, high-stakes environments, not just look good in a presentation. From there I moved into consulting, then product management, then delivery leadership across multi-country technology centres, and eventually programme ownership inside a product company. Along the way I've managed large delivery portfolios across the US, UK, MENA, APAC and India. I've navigated complex regulatory programmes and led AI adoption from early proof-of-concept through to production. The domain breadth matters to me. Payments, lending, trade finance, AML, fraud risk, core banking, credit risk, open banking. I've worked across all of them, in multiple geographies and regulatory frameworks. On the technology side, I've made a conscious choice to keep learning. Cloud-native platforms, DevOps, multi-cloud across AWS and GCP, AI and ML programme delivery. I hold 20+ active certifications because staying credible with engineering and architecture teams requires staying current. What I do, simply put: I help organisations deliver complex financial technology programmes. Through ambiguity, competing priorities, and regulatory pressure. In a way that holds up long after go-live. Currently open to Senior TPM, Program Director, and technology leadership roles. Open to relocation globally.

basic_profile.name: Ashu Pachauri
basic_profile.headline: Building - For Human Intelligence, Co-founder & Ex-CTO - Clarisights, Ex - Meta, Ex - Rocketfuel, HBase Committer
basic_profile.summary:
I have been building large scale distributed systems to tackle scale challenges, architecting deeply technical end-to-end systems to solve product challenges and fostering a culture of learning and perseverance to solve engineering challenges for the last 12+ years.

I am a student and a problem solver at heart. I am not tied to a specific piece of technology and believe fundamentally in using the right tool for the job. Similarly, I strongly believe in the idea of utilizing people to their strenghts while simulateneously nurturing them for the unknown. I have taken lots of decisions that have survivied the test of time and tons more that failed. In other words, I pride myself in having learnt my lessons through experience and prize both my successes and failures.

On a technical front, I have personally become intimately familiar with the rough edges of the Von Neumann architecture. I am initmately familiar with the challenges of building large scale distributed systems, be it the hardware performance characteristics,  or the internals of the networking stack or the right data structures to store and transfer data.  I have built, deployed and maintained end to systems ranging from the hardware to the UI, interacting with provisioning, configuration, development, testing, deployment and maintenance

I have created databases from scratch, managed them at petabyte scale. I have architected data orchestration and processing systems from zero,  evolved product backends and frontends, gone into the depths of existing large scale systems like Spark, HBase, Hadoop, Kubernetes,  Clickhouse etc. I have also touched the internals of Linux quite often, written toy kernels as fun projects and a strong believer in the power of curiosity and tinkering.

basic_profile.name: Eliza Auld
basic_profile.headline: Event Producer | Community Builder |  Founder -​> building the infrastructure for a sustainable arts ecosystem 💫
basic_profile.summary: Art is storytelling — and storytelling is the most enduring infrastructure humanity has. It's how we've built communities, shaped societies, and ultimately what has led us to be able to achieve the astonishing discoveries and inventions that we take advantage of in our day-to-day lives. An appreciation for that significance has shaped my entire career. Working across the arts industry in many capacities — from welcoming audiences front of house, to stoking the financial engine that keeps the house lights on, to building communities that are moved to keep showing up, I've spent years asking the same question: how do we build environments where art and its practitioners can actually thrive? That question led me to start a company. I'm founding a Public Benefit Corporation designed to close the gap between the commercial live experience world and arts institutions — combining the reach of one with the credibility of the other. At its core, this project is about access — for audiences, for artists, and for an industry that deserves better infrastructure than what exists today. If you're building in the arts & culture, live experience, or impact space, or you're someone who's deeply invested in what the arts can achieve — I'd love to connect.

basic_profile.name: Roy Yang
basic_profile.headline: Executive Leader | MBA | Entrepreneur
basic_profile.summary:
I obtained my MBA from University of Washington, BS in Electrical Engineering from University of California, Davis and MS in Electrical Engineering from Santa Clara University. 

In November 2021 I joined the Lam Search Corporation as Director of Pilot Manufacturing Management in their Fremont, CA plant, responsible for production related to the manufacturing of the company’s capital equipment, systems, components, sub assemblies, and subsystems.

In June of 2018 I joined the Boeing Zhoushan Completion Center in Zhoushan, China as the site engineer leader, responsible for manufacturing engineering, industrial engineering, liaison engineering, facility engineering, equipment engineering, and tool engineering functions. I am also responsible for the overall contract with the site integrated facility management service provider.

In July of 2014 I joined the Boeing Electrical Systems Responsibility Center as a production engineering manager responsible for product testing, tool engineering, and equipment engineering. 

My previous responsibility at the Boeing company was to work with internal clients from many disciplines such as Design, Manufacturing, Supplier Management, and Finance to provided integrated business process and tool solution, and generate better quality and visibility.

My other passion is employee involvement and development. I am trained and specialized in cross cultural communication and collaboration. I am a board member and the Vice President of Boeing internal affinity group specifically targeting employees of Asian and Pacific Island origin, and have organized numerous events throughout the year. I am the co-founder of the Boeing Leadership Education Program for Asian American Employees, which gave many Asian and non-Asian employees the necessary training and skill set to step up into leadership roles. My team was awarded the 2013 Boeing Diversity Change Agent award for our effort.

I am also involved in supporting local non-profit organization. I have been a chapter coordinator of the MATHCOUNTS foundation since 2009, helping to promote math in local schools.

Outside of work I love to spend time with family, travel, taste gourmet food, and watching my favorite professional and collegiate sport teams. I am an avid photographer. I have also been in training to get my Private Pilot's License.

basic_profile.name: Scott Evans
basic_profile.headline: Co-founder & CEO, ATRIUM | Former Microsoft VP & GM — HoloLens, Xbox, Windows | Board Chair, Finagraph (acquired) | Spatial Computing, AI, Gaming
basic_profile.summary: I build new product categories. Over 25 years I have worked across business, experience, and technology roles in gaming, spatial computing, enterprise, and government markets.  In parallel, I spent 13 of those years on the other side of the table as a board chair taking a venture-backed company to exit. At Microsoft for 24 years, most recently in Vice President & General Manager roles, I led product organizations behind HoloLens and Mesh, ran program management for the Xbox 360 platform and Kinect, and built Xbox Video into the second-largest video-on-demand service of its time. I started Microsoft's first-party Mixed Reality solutions business from zero, grew it to 150 people in its first year, and was deal lead on a Department of Defense program with a contract ceiling of $22 billion, a business later acquired by Anduril. Along the way I owned P&Ls from $20M to roughly $1B a year, led the acquisition and integration of Havok, built partner ecosystems with more than twenty tier-one ISVs, and created and taught one of the company's executive courses on strategic decision-making. In the venture world, I chaired the board of fintech startup Finagraph through two funding rounds, a strategic partnership with Moody's Analytics, and a private-equity-led exit that combined it with LeaseCrunch to form Crunchafi.  Since leaving Microsoft in 2024 I've closed the Finagraph sale, co-founded Atrium, taking it through prototype, and co-founded Third Village Society, a 501(c)(3) now running its second international cohort supporting girls' education in rural Cambodia.  Atrium is where my time goes now. We are building for the next generation of AR glasses at the intersection of sports and video games, more on that later this year.

basic_profile.summary: The world produces $118 trillion a year — about $14,400 per person. But a quarter must be reinvested just to keep the machine running, so even perfect redistribution delivers only ~$8,200 each. That's the ceiling of sharing itself. The pie, divided flawlessly, still isn't enough.Prosperity can't be redistributed. It has to be produced.So we chose a number: $10,000 a year. It exceeds what an equal share of the global economy could provide — meaning it can't be handed to you. If you earn it, you created it. Ten thousand dollars a year is the line where you stop dividing the pie and start growing it.AI & Robotics collapsed the cost of the tools of production. Atoma's mission is to put them in eight billion pairs of hands — so any human, regardless of geography, credentials, or capital, can create their first $10,000.And the floor is not the ceiling. Assets compound. A hundred thousand is what happens when you keep going.My company's mission is to help any human on Earth create their first $10,000. My mission is to show you the rest of the way — to $100,000+ a year from assets you own.

basic_profile.name: Vladimir Suhadolnik
basic_profile.headline: Father of Invited Advertising
basic_profile.summary: Welcome! I've been in business since the early 90s, working primarily as an entrepreneur or marketing consultant, advising Fortune 500 telecoms, energy/software/technology startups, and consumer product manufacturers. International experience includes online gaming as well as manufacturing electronics products overseas and bringing them to market through global retail channel partners. My career has provided opportunities to develop expertise in Design and Marketing/Advertising. Increasingly, it's obvious to me that technological innovation has changed the way businesses and consumers see one another. Ads are universally disliked by consumers who today see right through marketing and sales practitioners' veiled agendas. Brands and agencies cling to a past that Nielsen props up with smoke and mirrors. The game has changed. To me, this is an exciting time, and opportunities abound for those willing to conceive of a new game, and write the new rules. That is decidedly not for everybody, but because over the course of my life and career I've operated with the mindset, temperament, and disposition of an entrepreneur, I feel ready, willing, and perhaps better equipped than most. I am ambidextrous, so leverage both left and right-brained thinking for most every task or challenge I face. I'm a well-tested and creative problem solver (and a father of five boys), so I work well under pressure and there's not a lot that I haven't seen or can't handle with a sense of humor and humility. Today, I find meaning and purpose supporting two startups: one is out to change the way the world sees People With Disabilities, the other is out to disrupt the global advertising industry with something I call Invited Advertising. Stay tuned. I would love to hear from you if any of the above resonates; if you recognize the existential crises facing the business world, and have your own two cents about potential paths forward. Always up for a meaningful conversation. \V/

basic_profile.name: Hilary Palanza
basic_profile.headline: Founder and CEO | International Museum of Dance
basic_profile.summary:
Hilary Palanza is a multidisciplinary arts leader, nonprofit founder, and policy-driven strategist whose career sits at the intersection of culture, public impact, and organizational transformation. With more than fifteen years of executive leadership experience, she has built and led arts institutions, raised substantial philanthropic support, and advanced equitable arts policy across multiple regions.

Hilary began her career in San Francisco, where she not only performed professionally but quickly moved into leadership roles that shaped local arts ecosystems. In 2009, she founded the Children’s Center for Dance—which grew to serve over 2,000 children—and Palanza Dance, her award-winning performing arts company. Recognizing the need for stronger infrastructure in the arts sector, Hilary earned a Master’s in Public Affairs from UC Berkeley’s Goldman School of Public Policy, adding rigorous training in governance, budgeting, public systems, and policy design to her arts expertise.

Her policy background fueled her work as a nonprofit development consultant, where she strengthened operational systems, secured funding, and supported sustainability planning for organizations including Alonzo King LINES Ballet, NDI-NM, and several community-embedded cultural programs. Hilary has a proven track record of building organizations from the ground up, architecting strategic plans, designing multi-year funding pipelines, and leading teams through growth and transition.

As the Founder and Chief Creative Officer of the International Museum of Dance (IMOD), Hilary has led the organization from concept to national visibility—securing more than $1.2M in funding and 3M in in-kind partnerships, designing innovative public programming, and building partnerships with schools, festivals, museums, and global dance leaders. She has stewarded IMOD through its foundational years as a 100% volunteer-powered nonprofit, establishing governance structures, managing budgets, overseeing operations, and shaping IMOD’s long-term strategic vision and organizational culture.

Hilary is widely regarded as a visionary arts executive who blends creativity, administrative discipline, policy insight, and deep community engagement to strengthen the cultural sector and expand access to the arts.

basic_profile.name: Akshay Andhare
basic_profile.headline: Mechanical Engineer building AI Systems for Real-World Problems
basic_profile.summary: I’m a mechanical engineer with 8+ years of experience across automotive product development, e-mobility, and digital engineering—working at companies like Cummins and Mahle.My journey started with core engineering problems: vibration, fatigue, powertrain systems, and high-performance engines. Over time, I moved closer to where engineering meets intelligence—leading simulation-driven development in e-mobility and working on systems like EV powertrains, thermal management, and next-generation energy solutions.What changed for me wasn’t just the domain, but the approach.I became deeply interested in how engineering systems can evolve from static designs to adaptive, intelligent systems. That led me into Digital Twin thinking—combining simulation, data, and predictive modeling to create systems that don’t just perform, but learn and improve.Today, my focus is shifting further into AI-driven engineering.I’m exploring how AI agents, local LLMs, and system-level intelligence can be integrated into real-world engineering workflows—moving beyond dashboards and analytics into decision-making systems that can act, optimize, and assist autonomously.I’m particularly interested in:- AI + physical systems (Digital Twins evolving into intelligent systems)  - Simulation + AI-driven optimization  - Agent-based engineering workflows  - Building practical, real-world AI applications  At the core, I enjoy working at the intersection of systems, intelligence, and real-world impact—where engineering is not just about design, but about building adaptive, future-ready systems.

current.employer_name: National Institutes of Health (NIH): Intramural Research Program (IRP)
current.employer_linkedin_description: The Intramural Research Program (IRP) is the internal research program of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), known for its synergistic approach to biomedical science. With 1,200 Principal Investigators and more than 4,000 Postdoctoral Fellows conducting basic, translational, and clinical research, the IRP is the largest biomedical research institution on Earth. Its unique funding environment means the IRP can facilitate opportunities to conduct both long-term and high-impact science that would otherwise be difficult to undertake. More than 50 buildings on NIH campuses are devoted to the research enterprise, from state-of-the-art animal care facilities to homes for 7-Tesla MRIs and confocal microscopes, to a neurosciences cluster designed to foster collaborations across disciplines. Our 240-bed research hospital is devoted to clinical research protocols.With rigorous external reviews ensuring that only the most outstanding research secures funding, the IRP is responsible for many scientific accomplishments, including the discovery of fluoride to prevent tooth decay, the use of lithium to manage bipolar disorder, and the creation of vaccines against hepatitis, Haemophilus influenzae (HIB), and human papillomavirus (HPV).

basic_profile.name: Fjodor Davidis
basic_profile.headline: Innovative Educator | Building what learning should feel like 🎓
basic_profile.summary: I work at the intersection of education, strategy, entrepreneurship, and emerging technologies. My core background is in education. I am a qualified secondary school teacher with a teaching degree from LMU Munich and practical teaching experience at several grammar schools. My academic path has also been shaped by international experience, including studies abroad in Australia supported by a highly selective PROMOS scholarship from the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD), awarded to top 2-3% of high-performing students based on academic excellence, motivation, and engagement. This broadened my perspective on education, learning cultures, and how students build confidence across systems. In addition, I served as a lecturer at the Munich Center for Teacher Education at LMU, designing and teaching sessions on “learning how to learn,” a field that has become one of my strongest professional interests. For many years, I have supported students in mathematics, English, business & law, French, and learning strategies. My focus has always been on helping students understand not only what to learn, but also how to learn more effectively. After serving as Head of Pedagogy at a tutoring startup, I am currently building something new in EdTech, still in stealth mode 🤫 but driven by a clear belief: learning should become simpler, more structured, and more effective. Because simple learns better. Alongside education, I bring an analytical and business-oriented background. A high school project that grew to 10,000 monthly users, HyperBlu aggregated news from a range of outlets including but not limited to CNN, Fox News, Al Jazeera, BBC, Times of India, and CGTN, and applied natural language processing with spaCy to filter out bias. Our core idea was to fuse news from tens of outlets together and then determine what we called an 'aggregate news feed' to strip out bias that comes from using just a few sources. past.employer_linkedin_description: LumArray, Inc. is developing a tool for microlithography that based on technology that was developed over the course of several years in the NanoStructures Laboratory at MIT. The technology is called Zone-Plate-Array Lithography (ZPAL). In contrast to the lithography techniques used in the semiconductor industry and in research, namely optical-projection lithography (OPL) and contact lithography (CL), LumArray's ZPAL tool does not employ a mask; that is, it is "maskless." This enables rapid turn around on designs and economic manufacturing when only small volumes are requires.

basic_profile.name: Dave Veale
basic_profile.headline: Professionally Offensive
basic_profile.summary:
Seasoned offensive cyber operator and leader. Having been a part of several top tier offensive teams, I have the benefit of exposure to diverse perspectives regarding the mission and execution of offensive operations. I am a major proponent for adversary emulation and empowering teams to adopt levels of technical tradecraft and aggressiveness akin to threat actors. My philosophy is that an offensive assessment may be the final opportunity to illuminate security gaps before an adversary attempts the same; the ability to provide clients unbiased insights into their systems' unique vulnerabilities could be the difference between a successful defense and an adversary's action on objectives.

I am fortunate to possess a positive, inquisitive, and tenacious nature. I regularly conceive of novel innovation, both hardware and software, and do my best to bring them into reality either through personal learning and initiative or by leveraging my network of technical experts. 'Where there's a will, there's a way' has proven true time and time again in regards to emerging technology. That motivates me to think outside the box and to take novel approaches to complex problems. Offensive security is a team effort; sharing knowledge with veterans and enthusiasm with newcomers is the foundation of a successful program. I am grateful everyday to have this passion in my life and for the opportunity to look forward to what the next day holds.

I'm Sneha. I started at AfterMarkett in sales helping them close more clients. My daily work involves talking to brands, understanding their needs, and helping them reach the right people.

WHERE DO WE START?How about Kansas City? That’s our home. That’s where Garmin put a stake in the ground in 1989. But some things won’t ever change: Our entrepreneurial spirit and a culture where everyone’s opinion matters. That’s because we believe it’s possible to light the tech world on fire and still be on a first name basis.BIG IDEAS, SMALL EGOSWhat we do best is make products that let our customers do what they love. To do that, we focus on practical innovation, never losing sight of the benefits our products bring to our customers. Sure, we love bells and whistles. What leading technology company doesn't? But we make sure ours have purpose. It’s not about the things we make. It’s about the things we make possible.WE’RE GLOBAL, SERIOUSLY.Yeah, we’re based in Kansas City, but we are truly a global company. With offices throughout Europe, Asia, Middle East, South America and Australia, our products are sold all over the world. One elevator ride at our headquarters and you’re likely to hear 4 (or more) different languages being spoken. At Garmin, we may act local, but we think global.DREAM BIG. SLEEP WELL.At Garmin, we like to encourage dreamers. But at some point it’s nice to wake up and enjoy a fully aware life. So we make it super easy to achieve a good balance between working, dreaming and enjoying life—from workout classes offered throughout the day, breaks to get out and move on our campus, and wellness programs offered throughout the year. It’s almost impossible not to take advantage of Garmin’s work-life balance opportunities.

Criar o projeto de branding da Barbearia Tradicional em 2012 e colocá-lo em prática foi um grande aprendizado como designer e como empreendedor. 
Desenvolver serviços e produtos de excelência sempre foi a premissa da nossa empresa. Por meio de gestão profissional e processos de design, criamos uma comunicação que funcionou ao longo dos anos. Vi de perto como uma experiência do cliente bem planejada gera resultados para todos os envolvidos. Uma comunicação visual bem estrutura e coesa fez com que nossa empresa se mantivesse líder de mercado na região por quase uma década. 
Tive a oportunidade de colocar em prática diversas disciplinas de design, marketing e gestão em um mesmo projeto, com um mesmo objetivo. Desde a decoração interna e os elementos sensoriais dentro do espaço física da empresa, até materiais gráficos, uniformes, protocolos de atendimento, manutenção das mídias digitais, UX e UI de produtos corporativos, criação de conteúdo áudio-visual, apresentações multimídia para equipe e investidores, diagramação e redação de texto, criação de campanhas anuais de marketing. Ganhei muita experiência por ter criado e implementado todos os eixos que compõe a experiência do cliente e isso me deixou muito realizado como profissional.
Com tudo isso em prática, somados à uma equipe de qualidade e bem treinada, a Barbearia Tradicional se tornou uma marca sinônimo qualidade e seriedade.

past.employee_description:
Durante 3 anos e 2 meses na Payface, fintech especializada em pagamentos por reconhecimento facial, atuei como um dos principais líderes da empresa em momentos críticos de expansão, contribuindo diretamente para seu crescimento estratégico e operacional.

Quando ingressei em 2021, a Payface estava no estágio Seed, com 20 colaboradores. Como Head de Design e Marketing, liderei iniciativas como:

Reformulação do branding, com foco na humanização da marca e uso de cores vibrantes.
Desenvolvimento dos pitch decks de investimento, colaborando com os founders para construir um case de sucesso que alavancou a captação de recursos.
Com o crescimento acelerado, a Payface alcançou 100 colaboradores, consolidando-se como referência no setor. Durante essa fase, fui alocado exclusivamente como Head de Design de Produto, liderando a estruturação completa da área. Minhas principais realizações incluíram:

Implementação de processos e ferramentas de UX/UI, focados nos desafios de usabilidade do reconhecimento facial no varejo físico.
Definição de diretrizes estratégicas de design e estruturação de squads alinhados às demandas do mercado.
Desenvolvimento do branding e identidade visual da nova vertical antifraude, voltada para bancos e grandes empresas.
Gerenciando duas verticais de design e equipes multidisciplinares, implementei iniciativas data-driven e apresentei resultados estratégicos em comitês de alinhamento. Minha liderança foi decisiva para impulsionar a cultura de design e a escalabilidade dos processos, refletindo diretamente no impacto e na competitividade da empresa.

Essa experiência consolidou minha expertise em liderança, planejamento, gestão de conflitos, UX design, inovação em um ambiente dinâmico e altamente competitivo, contribuindo para o sucesso e crescimento da Payface e Fortface.

basic_profile.summary:
Ethical technologist, engaged with net-positive solutions on global, national, and local scales for ~20 years. Trained directly by pioneers of the early internet, personal computing, ecology movement, 'green' infrastructure & energy, distributed networking protocols, P2P, VR, virtual community, digital design, interactive media, AI, cyberlaw, B-corp law, climate finance & 'multi-bottom line' capitalism. Third-generation 'green' businessman, son and grandson of pioneers in the field. Familial relationship to the origins of venture capital. 

Raised in the intellectual rigor & gestalt of Harvard & MIT. From age 16, chose a path of apprenticeship, action learning, & autodidactism, pursuing no formal education. 

Initially trained for a contemplative life in Buddhist practice until late 20's. Was the youngest founding member of the Interspiritual Dialogue group under the U.N. Spiritual Caucus. From retreat wrote the group's successful application to the World's Parliament of Religions in Barcelona in 2004. Entered the  fray age 29, & since served in dozens of missions, commercial & non-profit, local & global, aiming to improve the world, and people's experience of it. Work has to date covered 15 of the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals.

Practiced as counsel, product & interface designer, creative director, solution finder, coder-herder, speaker, & author. Knowledge-of-the-larger-shape-of-things mixed with gritty applied experience. 

In 2009, corralled, co-authored, co-designed, & published the germinal 700-page encyclopedia of the commons & collaboration, exploring implications of the internet, P2P, & open source development protocols & ethos on the future of economy, business, and governance as we aim to solve the social, technological, & ecological crises of our time. Book foresaw basic features & emerging trends of our contemporary world. 

Through this book first met John Perry Barlow, later becoming Barlow's knight's apprentice & consigliere, In a a form of post-doc-meets-bond-mission-meets-gonzo-finishing-school. Currently Barlow's primary archivist.

Special assistant to Ted Nelson,  original visionary of the Web, hypertext, and the personal computer. Re-examining all standard assumptions about computing , databases, and the Internet.

Aims to assist highly competent teams building net-positive products. Applies informed ingenuity, cross disciplinary overview, privileged access, & uncommon lived experience to thwart dystopia. Maintains a sense of humor, while being deeply aware of the odds and stakes. Generally up for a conversation.

Continuing action research in the foundations of computing, networked computing, and the internet, with a pioneer of pioneers. Inventor of hyperlinks, the "back button", and generally considered the original visionary of the global hypertext system we commonly call the Internet, this all In addition to writing the first book on the personal computer "Computer Lib". A rabbit hole of "firsts", more than can be written here. Brilliant, eccentric, understandably ornery. 

To give a sense of the place in lineage to newer netizens, the very first page on the world wide web (www.), Tim Berners Lee's page at CERN, credited only two names. Both of them were Ted Nelson. Just to realize that "http" was a convenient reduction of possibilities is startling in and of itself.

Its fair to say that in our work together, a number of arbitrary yet persistent concepts about how computers and networked computing can operate (views held dear and unquestioned by just about everyone as far as the eye can see), go "poof!" every day. Incredibly helpful for approaching recalcitrant problems in new ways. 

Currently addressing among other things... ZigZag, an early form of hyperdimensional database, and its visualization. And yes, Xanadu. Turns out it's real, interesting, and relevant... not just archaic vaporware :)

past.employer_linkedin_description: The Berkeley City Club is a historic hotel, private social club, event space, and fine dining restaurant. It has been accepted into the National Register of Historic Places and is a member of the Historic Hotels of America. In 1927, a small group of women felt the need for a center around women’s activities and had cherished the plan of bringing this into being in Berkeley. These women hired Julia Morgan to design and supervise the construction of the Club, also known as the “Little Castle” since Miss Morgan was also building the Hearst Castle and many of the buildings' features remind visitors of the Hearst Castle. Upon opening in November 1930, it was the Berkeley Women’s City Club, which became a center for social, cultural, recreational, and family activities in the East Bay. At the height of its legacy as a social club, there were 4,000 female members. In 1965, the club opened its door to both men and women. The membership legacy continues to thrive as a hub for social, business, and cultural interaction.

basic_profile.summary:
Over a thirty-year professional career, I've been involved in over 150 transactions with clients all over the world in mandates requiring professional expertise in a wide variety of Capital Market, Business Advisory and/or Venture Scaling services. I've served as a "Consultant" to National & Provincial Governments, as an "Advisor" to Billion-Dollar Domestic & Multinational Corporations and as a "Mentor" to Zero-Dollar startups & first-time Entrepreneurs.

My experience spans the entire spectrum of value-creation in the entrepreneurial and business worlds, ranging from: (i) the raising of seed-round capital for fledgling start-ups, (ii) the syndication of IPO-round capital for high-growth businesses, (iii) mezzanine-round and/or PIPE capital for mature businesses, to (iv) full liquidity and redemption-round capital in the outright sale and/or M&A of stage-agnostic businesses. 

A keen student of excellence in Business-Management and Business-Leadership, I have had the privilege of working with some of the most iconic business brands in the world and the honour of working with some of the most iconic business leaders in the world. In doing so, I have borne first-hand witness to the essential and undeniable truism of Drucker's wisdom about "Management" and "Leadership;" namely, that "management is doing things right" and "leadership is doing the right things." 

Accordingly, I have also borne first-hand witness to intrepid start-up CEOs turning their struggling ventures into billion-dollar enterprises because they chose to do the right things and their managers did things right, while also witnessing complacent (and/or corrupt) CEOs turning their billion-dollar businesses into rubble because they chose to do the wrong things and their management, in turn, accelerated the entity's downfall by doing things wrong. 

Presently, as I enter the third-quarter of my career, I seek to bring the sum-total of my professional abilities in alignment with my personal passions, so as to: (a) help conceive, build, scale and exit a select number of high-impact businesses, (b) raise capital and/or invest in a very small number of social-impact ventures, and (c) continue to serve as an Advisor to a limited number of for-profit and nonprofit organizations. I also intend to continue volunteering my time in education, animal-rights, pet-welfare & conservation related activities.

As a Freelance Computer Vision Engineer, I design production-ready systems that bridge research with real-world needs. My work helps clients in healthcare, education, aviation, and enterprise automate workflows, improve accuracy, and scale reliably.

    • OpenCV pipelines: preprocessing, contour/shape detection, thresholding, noise filtering.

    • Deep learning with YOLO frameworks for detection, classification, and segmentation.

📌 Value Delivered

    • Reduced errors with advanced calibration and geometric correction.
    • Delivered marker-tracking systems for robotics and navigation.
    • Boosted analytics with custom detection and segmentation models.

Poor calibration, tracking drift, or misclassification can break automation and cost businesses time, money, and safety. My role as a Computer Vision freelancer is to de-risk deployments with reliable, optimized, and scalable solutions.

Organizations in healthcare, education, aviation, and enterprise rely on my expertise to turn vision challenges into measurable business value.

basic_profile.summary:
Product & Growth Leader. I love building user-focused products that solve problems and help businesses grow.

Proven expertise in unbolting growth for businesses across HR-Tech, Ed-Tech, E-Commerce, Clean-Tech, E-Mobility, and Fin-Tech industries at scale ($XXX Mn). Now accelerating Product led Growth for a Fintech building payments product(s) for 120 Mn+ MSMEs/SMBs in India.

Process oriented thinker at the core, I am passionate about creating repeatable playbooks & delivering results that improve the bottom-line. Having built & led high-quality cross-functional teams, I am efficient at leading such groups to plan, build, launch & manage world class products.

I balance operational rigour with a strong bias towards execution & innovation.

As an entrepreneur in the past, I had co-founded 3 companies- Get My Vape (E-Commerce) & The Amateur Tutors Club (Career Mentoring, and Educational Coaching) & DeliverE (Clean-Tech). As an Operator (product builder), I have built an electric scooter, & created an AI powered product for Math educators across the globe.

I created & launched India's first & biggest vaping marketplace- Get My Vape. During my time at Get My Vape, I was conferred with the award of building India's most unique consumer internet startup driving high social impact (Hot100 Tech Startup). Earned a Forbes 30 under 30 Nomination, graduated out of Global Startup Ecosystem 1st Cohort (ranked 1st) & was ranked as one of the Great Companies in the SMB category.

At college, I started a community to democratise the early careers of non-technical grads. Before college, I spent 2 years building a product to simplify hiring for IT/ITeS firms.

Areas of expertise:-

1. Product Ownership: Planning, Roadmap, Launch & Management
2. GTM Strategy, Business Growth
3. Product led Growth
4. P&L Management, Process Design & Improvement
5. Data Analysis- SQL, A/B Testing, Google Analytics
6. MS Excel, Agile & Scrum Methodologies, JIRA
7. Public Speaking & Mentoring

Outside of work, I engage in outdoor sports, love traveling, read & learn about emerging technologies, innovations, and frameworks. I mentor early-stage startups, speak about entrepreneurship, and building winning products. I’ve given over a dozen talks and judged various entrepreneurial competitions at various Tech & Business Schools in India.

My passion is to build highly scalable & futuristic product led businesses to solve mankind's greatest challenges & my long-term vision is to empower every person and organisation to achieve more. Let’s connect!

basic_profile.summary: 🚀 𝐒𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐚𝐥 𝐄𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐞𝐩𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐮𝐫 | 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐡𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 & 𝐓𝐞𝐜𝐡 | 𝐌𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐨𝐫 𝐟ü𝐫 𝐖𝐚𝐜𝐡𝐬𝐭𝐮𝐦Ich bin 𝐍𝐢𝐜𝐨 𝐒𝐜𝐡𝐮𝐛𝐞𝐫𝐭 – Unternehmer, Gründer und Mentor mit über 13 Jahren Erfahrung in 𝐑𝐞𝐜𝐫𝐮𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠, 𝐁𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐃𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐥𝐨𝐩𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐮𝐧𝐝 𝐔𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐞𝐡𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐭𝐮𝐦.Gestartet bin ich 2013 in 𝐄𝐧𝐠𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐝, wo ich klassisches Headhunting von Grund auf gelernt habe: Outbound-Suche, Telefon-Recruiting, Business Development. Danach habe ich in einer 𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐧 𝐏𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥𝐛𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐮𝐧𝐠 eine Schlüsselrolle übernommen und den Aufbau des deutschen Standorts maßgeblich mitgestaltet. Ich habe die Expansion mit Standorten in 𝐃𝐞𝐮𝐭𝐬𝐜𝐡𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐝, 𝐄𝐧𝐠𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐮𝐧𝐝 𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥 maßgeblich begleitet – die Unternehmensgruppe wuchs in dieser Zeit auf über 𝟓𝟎𝟎 𝐌𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐛𝐞𝐢𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐞 𝐰𝐞𝐥𝐭𝐰𝐞𝐢𝐭.Als HR-Manager und Teamleiter habe ich 𝐌𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐛𝐞𝐢𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐞 𝐚𝐮𝐬𝐠𝐞𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐝𝐞𝐭, 𝐓𝐞𝐚𝐦𝐬 𝐰𝐞𝐢𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐰𝐢𝐜𝐤𝐞𝐥𝐭 und gleichzeitig als einer der erfolgreichsten Headhunter hunderte Fach- und Führungskräfte vermittelt.Darauf aufbauend habe ich mehrere eigene Recruiting- und Tech-Unternehmen gegründet – ich bin 𝐮. 𝐚. 𝐆𝐫ü𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐕𝐄𝐑𝐓𝐀𝐗 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐮𝐩 𝐆𝐦𝐛𝐇, dem 𝐆𝐨𝐥𝐝𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐫𝐝 𝐢𝐧 𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐏𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐦𝐢𝐭𝐭𝐥𝐮𝐧𝐠 𝐟ü𝐫 𝐒𝐭𝐞𝐮𝐞𝐫𝐛𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐮𝐧𝐠𝐬𝐠𝐞𝐬𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐬𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐧 in Deutschland. Mit VERTAX haben wir:innerhalb von 12 Monaten einen 𝟕-𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐠𝐞𝐧 𝐔𝐦𝐬𝐚𝐭𝐳 erzieltüber 𝟑.𝟎𝟎𝟎 𝐊𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐞 erschlossendas Team von 𝟏 𝐚𝐮𝐟 𝟏𝟓 𝐌𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐛𝐞𝐢𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐞 skaliertNeben Recruiting treibe ich die Entwicklung von 𝐝𝐢𝐠𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐧 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐭𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐞𝐧 & 𝐀𝐈-𝐋ö𝐬𝐮𝐧𝐠𝐞𝐧 voran, arbeite an neuen Geschäftsmodellen und teile mein Wissen als 𝐌𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐨𝐫 𝐟ü𝐫 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐡𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫 & 𝐔𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐞𝐡𝐦𝐞𝐫, die schneller wachsen und ihre Umsätze vervielfachen wollen.💡 𝐌𝐞𝐢𝐧 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐳𝐢𝐩: 100 % Ownership. Klare Prozesse. Messbare Ergebnisse.🌍 𝐌𝐞𝐢𝐧𝐞 𝐒𝐜𝐡𝐰𝐞𝐫𝐩𝐮𝐧𝐤𝐭𝐞:-High-Performance Recruiting & Executive Search-Unternehmertum & Business Scaling-AI & Tech im Recruiting-Leadership & Extreme Ownership👉 𝐋𝐚𝐬𝐬 𝐮𝐧𝐬 𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐞𝐭𝐳𝐞𝐧, wenn du:📩 als 𝐊𝐚𝐧𝐳𝐥𝐞𝐢 (𝐒𝐭𝐁/𝐖𝐏/𝐋𝐞𝐠𝐚𝐥) Top-Talente suchst🤝 als 𝐔𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐞𝐡𝐦𝐞𝐫:𝐢𝐧 / 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐡𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫 dein Business skalieren willst🚀 dich für 𝐀𝐈, 𝐓𝐞𝐜𝐡 & 𝐈𝐧𝐧𝐨𝐯𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 interessierst

Security teams today face a growing execution gap: attacks are becoming more sophisticated, security stacks are generating more alerts and tasks, and skilled cybersecurity talent remains limited.

We are building a workforce of AI cybersecurity experts, each specialized in a different security domain, working alongside human teams, operating across the existing security stack, and executing complex workflows end-to-end.

past.employer_linkedin_description: A Edenred é líder global em Benefícios & Engajamento e Mobilidade. Com mais de 1 milhão de empresas clientes em 44 países, sua plataforma conecta mais de 60 milhões de usuários aos serviços e produtos de mais de 2 milhões de estabelecimentos parceiros.A companhia oferece soluções digitais para colaboradores, incluindo alimentação, mobilidade, cartões-presente, bem-estar, recompensas e ofertas; para gestores de frotas, com soluções multienergia, recarga de veículos elétricos, manutenção, reembolso de IVA, pedágios e estacionamento; e para pagamentos corporativos, por meio de cartões virtuais.Guiadas pelo propósito da Edenred, “Enrich connections. Também ajudam a aumentar a atratividade e a eficiência das empresas, ao mesmo tempo em que impulsionam o mercado de trabalho e as economias locais.No Brasil, onde atua há 50 anos, a Edenred está presente na vida de milhões de trabalhadores e empresas por meio de soluções de Benefícios & Engajamento, Mobilidade e Pagamentos Corporativos. Somos uma Datatech, líder global em soluções de inteligência para análise de riscos e oportunidades com foco nas jornadas de crédito, autenticação e prevenção à fraude. Temos presença global com expertise local, estamos em 30 países e atuamos há 55 anos no mercado brasileiro. Contamos com os melhores talentos, mais de 21 mil colaboradores no mundo e quase 5 mil no Brasil.  Trabalhamos sempre para criar um ambiente diverso e equilibrado para todas as nossas pessoas. Por isso, temos tanto orgulho de estarmos sendo continuamente reconhecidos como uma das melhores empresas para se trabalhar pelo Great Place to Work, Linkedin e Employers for Youth. E não para por aí. Aqui, inovação é o nosso combustível e não é à toa que a gente sabe quem é quem. Temos o maior ecossistema de big data da América Latina e a ele somamos tecnologia de ponta para revelar o que nem todos conseguem ver e ir além do óbvio. Com um portfólio completo e flexível, enxergamos o todo e à frente. Antecipamos o futuro para oferecer a pessoas e empresas um caminho que transforme, hoje, a incerteza do risco na melhor decisão. É assim que ajudamos pessoas a realizarem seus sonhos e empresas a prosperarem. Que trabalhamos por um Brasil com mais inclusão financeira. Afinal, trabalhar na Serasa Experian é muito mais do que as pessoas imaginam. É criar um amanhã melhor para todos, ampliando oportunidades aqui e agora.

past.employer_linkedin_description: O conceito do California Coffee® nasceu quando visitamos o Brasil. Uma questão nos surpreendeu. Porque o maior exportador de café do mundo, que produz um café tão fino e de alta qualidade, não tem a oportunidade de saborear o melhor do que produz? A resposta é muito simples: A maioria da produção dos melhores e mais finos cafés é vendida para a exportação. Os fundadores do California Coffee® decidiram, então, trazer a idéia de "Specialty Coffee House" para o Brasil. California Coffee® oferece apenas a melhor classe de café arábica, cultivado em regiões especialmente selecionadas. Lá o café é plantado em grandes altitudes, o que leva a um crescimento mais lento e a um sabor mais fino. O nosso café é selecionado a partir dos melhores grãos de exportação.California Coffee® se destaca por ser intransigente quanto a qualidade, o frescor e o serviço personalizado e reconhecido. Nossa meta é garantir o melhor copo de café possível, sem levar em consideração o custo ou o esforço exigido. Torrado o nosso café artesanalmente de acordo com os mais rígidos padrões europeus em nossa própria torrefação. Trabalhando continuamente para melhorar a qualidade e a consistência do café para trazer o melhor de cada grão para você.Finalmente, o maior produtor mundial já pode beber o mesmo café servido nos mais finos Coffee Shops do mundo.California Coffee®, no Brasil desde 2002.

basic_profile.name: Andrew Ellam
basic_profile.headline: Co-Founder at Stealth Mode Startup
basic_profile.summary:
Started as a software engineer. Scaled systems at Amazon and Meta. Now sit on Ofgem's decision enforcement panel for UK energy infrastructure. Most recently Interim CTO at Previsico (Series A, ML/physics platform serving insurers).

Technical depth
25 years in technology, hands-on throughout. Founded and ran profitable technology businesses for 14 years - designed systems, wrote code, shipped product. At Climate X, owned architecture for ML/physics platform serving major financial institutions; cut AWS costs 50%; accelerated releases from quarterly to 3x/week (36x). At Previsico, made architectural decisions for real-time data pipelines. AWS Solutions Architect Professional. ML training (Stanford, DeepLearning.AI).

Delivery at scale
At Meta, led 18-month cross-company program with Google (150 people, multiple countries) generating over $1bn annual revenue. Ran 21 concurrent projects for Facebook Shops. At Amazon Video, designed readiness framework coordinating 35 engineering teams across US, Europe, and Asia to validate 150 services for peak-traffic events. Incident controller for major launches.

Regulated environments
Ofgem Enforcement Decision Panel member (2023-present): decisions on critical energy infrastructure, setting multi-million pound fines. Regulatory panel experience since 2015 across three UK regulators. At Monzo (FCA/PRA-regulated), briefed Board on cloud strategy and operational resilience; defined multi-cloud architecture options; negotiated multi-million pound contracts with AWS and GCP. Represented bank at Bank of England and UK Finance.

Team building
Scaled engineering from 3 to 15 at Climate X; from 6 to 15 at Previsico - managing both IC engineers and engineering managers. Built team of 8 Technical Program Managers at Meta. Created competency frameworks, career levels, salary bands, performance management. Supported $18M Series A due diligence on team capability. Improved team gender diversity from 0% to 27%.

Investor perspective
Angel investor in 93 tech startups since 2017. Pattern recognition across fintech, climate tech, and software infrastructure.

Speaker: SREcon 2022 (cloud operational resilience), CTO Craft 2024 (influencing senior stakeholders).

basic_profile.name: Michael Shin, CAMS
basic_profile.headline: Chief Compliance Officer at Loop | Building AI-native compliance infrastructure in stealth
basic_profile.summary: I started building on the internet at 13. I taught myself HTML, created community and entertainment websites, learned distribution by submitting them to early search engines, and earned US$200 to US$500 per month from overseas advertising networks before I understood what a startup was. At 16, I moved alone from Korea to Canada without family or an existing network. That experience taught me to solve problems without waiting for permission, become comfortable with rejection, and keep moving until I found a path forward. I later spent more than 18 years in banking, payments, crypto, and fintech, progressing from an AML investigator at BMO to Chief Compliance Officer and Head of Compliance roles. I have built AML programs, regulatory frameworks, risk and control systems, and compliance operations for regulated financial products.  Along the way, I worked inside both large financial institutions and early-stage companies. I helped launch regulated products, worked with banks and regulators across jurisdictions, and led teams responsible for compliance, operations, and growth.  Today, I am now building in stealth at the intersection of AI, financial compliance, and regulated operations.I believe AI creates an unusual opportunity for domain experts. Problems that previously required large engineering teams and significant capital can now be translated directly into working software by people who understand the underlying workflows, risks, and customer needs.My view is that AI should not replace accountable human judgment. It should remove the repetitive analysis, coordination, documentation, and maintenance surrounding the decisions for which professionals must remain accountable.I cannot control luck, but I can increase the chances of encountering it by continuing to build, ask, and show up. After nearly two decades in regulated finance, I am returning to what I enjoyed most at 13: learning a new technology, building something useful, and taking it to market. This time, I understand the problem, the industry, and the customer. This time, I intend to take it all the way.

Sound like you and I have something to discuss?

Feel free to DM me directly, or book a call on my calendar. 
Always happy to have a listen.

past.employee_description:
I founded the NUESA Academic Platform as a nonprofit academy to assist students in our faculty who were struggling academically. We built the system around the Socratic method of teaching, which revolves around asking questions to stimulate critical thinking and learning.

Our approach was simple: we grouped students based on their courses and academic levels, and each week, we provided them with a set of questions designed to test what they had learned so far. Students were expected to answer these questions and raise any additional ones they had. Their peers often voluntarily helped answer, and when needed, the coordinator of NAP stepped in to provide further clarity.

This initiative supported about 2,000 first- and second-year students across various departments, including science, technology, arts, social sciences, education, and foundational counseling. It not only helped them prepare for exams and review lessons but also fostered peer learning and collaboration. For new students who were still adapting to university life, it was an opportunity to get extra support without any additional cost.

Unfortunately, after I completed my program, the platform had to shut down. The level of interest and the heavy management it required made it unsustainable without ongoing involvement.

We founded Lavender Tutors as a social enterprise in Nigeria with the goal of supporting poor and underperforming secondary school students who were falling behind in one subject or another. Our research showed that the average Nigerian classroom has 15-30 students, each with different backgrounds, interests, and learning speeds. It became clear that many students struggled in certain subjects, while excelling in others. Yet, the school system often assumes that all students should learn at the same pace, without providing adequate support for those who lag behind after the traditional 45-minute lessons.
Our vision for Lavender Tutors was to create a team of passionate educators dedicated to helping each student improve in their weaker areas, with the hope that they would eventually grow to love the subject and pursue it further. 
While it might sound like a regular tutorial service, our approach was more specialized. We assessed each student's unique challenges and provided tailored solutions, much like a medical specialist diagnosing and treating a specific issue. Additionally, we partnered with schools to track each student's progress and ensure they were improving.
We designed Lavender Tutors to be accessible to low-income students by implementing systems like the "1 for 1" payment model, allowing us to support those in need. In 2022, we decided to transition from a brick-and-mortar operation to a digital platform, which is now known as LearnPlanet.

basic_profile.headline: Inventor, physicist & startup founder | Dedicated to improving the world that we live in
basic_profile.summary: Brandon's mission is simple: to commercialize new and transformative technologies that solve real-world problems. This mission led to Akadeum Life Sciences, where he founded and led the company to being ranked the 5th Most Innovative Biotech, Best Workplace for Innovators by Fast Company, and 2025 Disruptive Technology of the Year Award at Advanced Therapies Week. Brandon is an award-winning entrepreneur, inventor, physicist, and customer discovery expert working with new technologies. His work has spanned eﬀorts in next-generation product launches, forming tech companies, research firsts, entrepreneurship education and venture capital. Brandon led Akadeum to being the first in the industry to develop microbubbles to capture and isolate cells, DNA and proteins for applications like cell therapy, diagnostics and research. The impact is that Akadeum leads the world with the most gentle and scalable technology.In other previous roles, including his position as a research faculty member in Biomedical Engineering at UM, he formed and led interdisciplinary research teams. Having performed award-winning research, Brandon received his PhD in Applied Physics from UM in 2007 and a BS in Physics from California State University Bakersfield in 2002.

basic_profile.headline: Stealth CTO
basic_profile.summary: Chat with me! https://book.gotsuss.ai/sidI’m a product-first engineering leader and founder with 7+ years of experience building and scaling consumer, payments, and AI products.I currently serve as Co-Founder & CTO of MotorFyx, an AI software platform for automotive service businesses. I lead product strategy, engineering, and go-to-market end-to-end, and have helped take the company from 0→1 to positive cash flow, raise $1M in funding, and expand to 85+ shop locations across California, Nevada, and Texas.On the technical side, I’ve built and deployed production AI agents across voice, SMS, and web chat; designed LLM retrieval, evaluation, and monitoring workflows; and built the underlying AWS, Node.js, and Next.js infrastructure supporting the platform. I also developed an autonomous marketing and AI-visibility engine spanning customer lifecycle messaging, paid acquisition, Google Business Profile, review generation, and attribution across traditional and AI search.Previously, I spent four years as a Software Engineer at Meta working across payments, growth, and platform infrastructure. My work included designing payment systems supporting approximately $1B in monthly transaction volume, building sanctions/KYC/AML infrastructure for Instagram payments, leading consumer rewards initiatives for MetaPay Wallet, and developing products that contributed to growth across Messenger, Facebook, and Instagram.Earlier in my career, I worked in autonomous-vehicle research at Berkeley DeepDrive and authored work published at IEEE IV. I also served as an Engineering Fellow with the Mobility Open Blockchain Initiative, where I led the architecture and authorship of the consortium’s first ratified decentralized vehicle identity standard.I’m especially interested in problems at the intersection of AI, product engineering, distributed systems, and zero-to-one product development—particularly where strong technical execution needs to translate directly into real customer and business outcomes.

basic_profile.name: Mark Belinsky
basic_profile.headline: Hardware & Software Product Innovation | Corporate & Government Strategy | Startup Founder
basic_profile.summary:
Building beautiful things that help lots of people is my driving passion.

Whether leading companies or driving product, I’m a creative technologist. I’m a big believer that beauty and efficiency drive results, both inside companies and with customers. I try to infuse this ethos across all divisions of an organization with agile methodologies and wonderful brand experiences. More often than not, I've worked with small teams under tight deadlines, meaning I can roll up my sleeves and dive into the trenches to execute in a variety of roles in order to get the exemplary results I demand of any project I lead.

My inspirations are leaders, from Benjamin Franklin to Muhammad Yunus, who fused technological innovation with creative inspiration, all while seeking to make a positive difference in the world. My voracious curiosity drives me to dive deep into any problem. I search beyond obvious ideas and work hard to determine the right blend of design, technology and strategy for a strong return on investment.

Spotting global trends early is one of my strengths and helps me promote solutions I'm enthusiastic about at the right time. From founding the nonprofit Digital Democracy in 2008 to now working as an innovation specialist at the United Nations Development Programme to integrate digital as a pillar of development, my ability to ideate and implement solutions to systemic, nascent problems, makes me a critical player in the human rights and innovation space.

Across domains like smart home IoT, interactive media, international development, sustainable tourism, product innovation, security and blockchain, I've raised venture capital funding, developed partnerships and represented companies in the media. I’ve shared these experiences as a speaker at SXSW, Tribeca Film Festival, and Hackers On Planet Earth, as a guest on BBC, Al-Jazeera, and NPR, lecturing at Harvard, Columbia and NYU, helping advise the Federal Reserve Bank of New York on blockchain technologies, and consulting with the US State Department, Fortune 500 companies, and several heads of state.

Above all, the specialities I most enjoy focusing my time on include business strategy, agile design, brand storytelling, public speaking, media production, and hardware + software development. I’m also big into biking absurdly long distances, love exploring new cuisines, and I make a solid Negroni.

past.employee_title: Head of Scaled Insight Science, Amazon Ads
past.employee_description:
I led a team that’s building a true data driven GTM engine.

Most sales organizations are designed “tops down”. You take some accounts, hire sales reps, and give them quota. Sophisticated organizations may use data to segment accounts, set the right quota, optimize account loads, and give sales people productivity tools. However the sales reps day to day activities are often a black box.

At Amazon Ads, my team is taking a different approach. We want to have a bottoms up model to give the optimal message at the optimal time to each advertiser. So we built a tool that provides autogenerated content to account teams for each advertiser each month using science. These are pre generated PPT decks that trigger when a ML model shows a meaningful opportunity, explains the opportunity to the advertiser, and delivers recommendations scientifically shown to capture the opportunity. We build tools to see how our account teams modify our content and how the customer responds. This creates a flywheel to help us understand all customer touch points and advertiser insights needed to make our advertisers successful. 

Once we have this (we power 20% of advertiser pitches now and are targeting 50% by end of 2023; $XXX hundred of millions in incremental revenue impact) we can build a truly data driven GTM engine. We will be to answer all of the Sales Data science questions (segmentation, lifecycle, account team composition, targets) in a truly bottoms up fashion while enabling granular performance management of our sales teams. We’ll also be able to add marketing and in product touch points to build a true data driven cross channel GTM engine.

NOTE: My official title started as "Head of Data Science, Field Sales", but the role quickly morphed into a data products role, so I am reflecting that on LinkedIn for simplicity

Civics Unplugged ("CU") is a 501(c)(3) shaping young leaders to build the future they want and deserve. Our programs prepare young leaders to design civic innovations—new ideas and technologies that solve community and civic problems. More than 6,000 high school students are now a part of a tight-knit CU community that transcends differences. The Fellows connect across political, geographic, racial, and socioeconomic lines, united by their commitment to leading with integrity and innovation. These young leaders will be our future founders, legislators, judges, journalists, and teachers, all collaborating to set up a brighter future for us all.The current education system is failing to prepare our country’s next generation to create a brighter future. In schools, we fail to help students be creative or develop entrepreneurial skills. As they grow up, we discourage them from pursuing their passions or taking on meaningful social impact work. Worst of all – we’ve created an environment where young people everywhere feel disconnected from their peers, their voice, and any form of civic agency. We believe the loneliness crisis Gen Zers face spurs directly from the lack of opportunities to do fulfilling civic work in communities across the country – and creates one of the biggest threats to our democracy we’ve ever faced. That’s why we built Civics Unplugged.

GENup is California’s largest youth-led education policy organization, engaging over 4,000+ student leaders from across the state that come from 85 K-12 public school districts as well as University of California and California State University institutions. GENup’s successes include working with the State Board of Education to create the State Seal for Civic Engagement, championing the historic ethnic studies bill (AB101) through the legislature & into law, fighting for equitable education funding during COVID, advocating for statewide mental health reform through legislation, successfully authoring/advocating/passing a bill into law on student board member rights (AB 824), campaigning for the U.S Department of Education’s first youth-advisory council, and passing (Los Angeles Unified, San Diego Unified, and Fresno Unified) first student bill of rights, collectively representing over 1.2 million students. In all, more than 46 education bills  GENup sponsored, authored, or wrote have been signed into law by Governor Newsom, including legislation requiring a mental health curriculum in all high school health education courses. GENup has become an influential youth-voice representing California’s students in the most pressing conversations on education policy, and our more than 100+ local chapters are an effective platform for grassroots student-led advocacy in our state.From top to bottom, GENup is for youth and by youth.

past.employer_linkedin_description: The Office of the Assessor-Recorder is responsible for fairly and accurately executing property assessment functions in accordance with the State Constitution and State and local laws. Our core responsibilities include identifying all taxable property in the City and County of San Francisco, establishing a taxable value, and applying all legal exemptions. Property broadly includes real property as well as personal property owned by businesses.The Office is also responsible for recording documents and securing public records. We ensure each document meets recording requirements and make them accessible to the public. We record over 400 different types of documents annually, including deeds of trust, reconveyances, liens, maps, and public marriage certificates. Additionally, the Office is responsible for collecting any transfer tax due upon a change in property ownership. We perform audits to ensure the correct property value basis for taxation. In all that we do we seek to advance the value of fairness, care, equity and excellence in service to our diverse constituents and communities.
